title: Epochal coalescer & backfill controller for low-latency console metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an epoch-based transaction coalescer and a coordinated backfill controller for the console metrics pipeline. Goal: reduce downstream write amplification and metric cardinality spikes while preserving strict per-tenant SLOs and enabling low-cost reconcilation for late-arriving events. The coalescer groups events into short-lived epochs (configurable 500ms-5s) per-tenant + route key, producing compact transactions with idempotency tokens. The backfill controller tracks epoch checkpoints and provides bounded, prioritized replays to correct missed or late data without blocking hotpath processing.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P99 ingest latency for 95% of tenants <= 120ms under nominal load
Write amplification to downstream storage reduced by >= 35% for metric heavy tenants
Backfill runs can replay up to 1 hour of missed epochs without exceeding per-tenant quota or breaching SLOs
Idempotent epoch tokens prevent double-counting in at-least-once delivery scenarios
Smoke tests, canary rollout, and monitoring dashboards are available before wide rollout
design_decisions: Use epoch boundaries instead of arbitrary batching to enable deterministic reconciliation
Tenant-local epoching: epochs anchored to logical tenant time windows to avoid cross-tenant interference
Store epoch checkpoints in a compact, append-only Kafka topic with key=tenant:route:epoch
Backfill controller runs as a low-priority consumer with rate-limits and soft-failures to protect hotpath
Prefer non-blocking KV cache updates and use eventual reconciliation to avoid increasing tail latency
tradeoffs_and_risks: Smaller epochs reduce reconciliation work but increase headroom for per-epoch metadata and coordination overhead
Epoch metadata increases metadata throughput; might need to offload compacted state to a tiered store
Backfill replays introduce tail load; must be strictly throttled to avoid SLO violations
Idempotency relies on stable tokens; schema changes or clock skew could complicate deduplication
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement tenant epocher + in-memory coalescer with feature flag
Phase 2 (1 week): durable epoch checkpoint writer and consumer-side idempotency checks
Phase 3 (2 weeks): backfill controller prototype with rate limiter and prioritization by tenant tier
Phase 4 (1 week): add observability (per-epoch counts, replays, latency histograms) and dashboards
Phase 5 (1 week): canary rollout to 10% of tenants, monitor, then progressive ramp to 100%
rollout_plan: Start with internal tenants + low-volume production customers
Canary: enable coalescer only (no backfill) for 10% traffic to verify latency/throughput
Enable backfill in dry-run mode (metrics only) for next 10% to validate reconciliation semantics
Full enable with conservative backfill throttles for remaining tenants if canary metrics stable for 48h
monitoring_and_slo: New dashboards: epoch-size distribution, coalesced write reduction, backfill queue depth
Alerts: spike in epoch lateness > 2s, sustained backfill latency > 60m, P99 ingest latency regressions > 10%
SLO targets to maintain: end-to-end P99 ingest latency baseline, 99.9% write correctness (no lost metrics)
testing_plan: Unit tests: epoch boundary calculus, idempotency token generation/validation
Integration: coalescer + checkpoint writer + backfill controller in staging with synthetic late-arrivals
Chaos: inject broker unreliability and out-of-order events to validate reconciliation
Load: benchmark under realistic tenant mix using existing traffic replay harness
